title: Auth lease mismatch causing quota misattribution and transient 429 cascade
creator: Mateo Singh
description: After a capacity bump and a configuration rollout on 2025-02-24 we observed a burst of 429s across several services. Investigation shows the rate limiter started enforcing quotas per token fingerprint that diverged between gateway nodes, resulting in over-counting and a transient 429 storm affecting hosted API customers. This ticket tracks the technical follow-ups, fixes, and monitoring required to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~22% of production tokens experienced intermittent 429s for 8–15 minutes during peak on 2025-02-24. Multiple customers reported degraded behavior (chat truncation, failed embeddings). No customer data was exposed. Financial impact estimated as short-lived request loss and increased retries; primary risk is customer trust and SLA breach potential.

2025-02-24 09:20 UTC - Rollback of previous quota routing config.
2025-02-24 10:03 UTC - Traffic stabilizes.

root_cause: Race between auth lease renewal and quota-shard mapping after a config rollout. TokenFingerprint generation differed between gateway versions (old nodes used token-hash v1, upgraded nodes used token-hash v2), causing the same logical token to be seen as multiple distinct keys by distributed quota shards. When shards later merged counters, duplicated counting across ephemeral shards produced effective over-usage, triggering 429s. A related bug: quota enforcer did not canonicalize legacy fingerprint variants before aggregation.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of quota routing change (done 2025-02-24)
Global soft-limit relaxation policy applied during incident to avoid mass 429s (temporary)
Emergency hotfix to canonicalize token fingerprint at the gateway edge (deployed canary 2025-02-26)
Add aggregation-by-user-id fallback in quota enforcer for 72 hours after node upgrades
